docs.text:
• Vehicle type: Pickup truck (double cab / 4-door)
  • Make/model: All suitable makes (Hilux, L200, Ranger, D-Max, Navara)
  • Budget: £5,000 (searched up to £5,500)

  • Defaults applied: Diesel preferred, Manual preferred (Ukraine deployment)
  • Search postcodes: BN1 1AL (1500mi radius = full UK coverage)
  • Platforms searched: AutoTrader (by make/model — Hilux, L200, Ranger, D-Max, Navara, Musso), Gumtree (by make/model — L200, Hilux, Ranger, D-Max), eBay Motors (by make/model — L200, Hilux, Ranger), CarGurus (returned SUVs not pickups — filter ineffective for commercial vehicles)

docs.title: Scoring System (Revised 2026-04-09)
docs.text:
Year and mileage are the most important factors — they are objective, verifiable, and directly predict remaining useful life. MOT data is treated asymmetrically: bad results (when found) are trustworthy and disqualify, but clean MOT history is NOT proof of condition — only a physical inspection can confirm that.

Factor Weight Scoring Year (age) 25% Newer = better. Objective, can't be faked. Mileage (absolute) 25% Lower = better. Verifiable via MOT mileage progression. Price (value) 20% Lower = better. Budget operation. Engine reliability 15% Based on engineering data, not one tester's opinion. MOT red flags 10% Disqualifier when bad. Mild positive when clean. Not proof. Location 5% Closer to Brighton = easier to inspect/collect.

2026-04-13 update: Prep estimates use cautious long-haul methodology — sized for a 2,500 mi / 3-day drive, includes MOT-flagged items + fresh fluids. Universal items (headlight stickers) and contingency removed from tables. Price sub-score uses landed cost.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Total vehicles found: ~90 across all makes (Hilux: 274, L200: 213, Ranger: 348 total results — most over budget)
  • Under £5,500 double cab diesel manual: ~26 (after completeness re-sweep)
  • MOT checked: 14 vehicles
  • Disqualified: 10 vehicles (7 MOT, 3 age)
  • Active candidates: 14 vehicles scored and ranked
  • Key finding: ALL Toyota Hiluxes in this price range have catastrophic structural corrosion. L200s fare much better.
  • Scoring note: Re-scored 2026-04-09 with year+mileage weighted 50% (previously MOT history was 20%). Clean MOT no longer treated as proof of quality.

docs.text:
• 2017 Mitsubishi L200, Bromley, £5,000 (FB 1960247451579087) — non-runner, engine knocking, needs rebuild/swap. Project only.
  • 2015 Mitsubishi L200, Bishop Auckland, £3,995 (FB 951321887634259) — single cab, not double cab.
  • 2006 Toyota Hilux Invincible, Bishop Auckland, £3,875 (FB 1691678171997749) — automatic + 3.0 D-4D 1KD-FTV (AMBER engine per manual). Two strikes.
  • Multiple obvious-scam listings (£1,700 2013 Ranger 2.2 limited London, £1,900 2016 Ranger 3.2 Luton, £2,500 2015 L200 Warrior Portsmouth, £4,499 2014 Hilux 12k mi Gamston, £2,400 2014 Hilux Invincible 57k London, £2,800 2016 Hilux 68k London, £1,700 2019 Hilux Walsall, £4,080 2021 Ranger Wildtrak Earls Barton). Pattern: post-2013 vehicles at <£3,000, often with implausibly low mileage. Per minibus search experience: "seller account joined in current year + price ~1/3 of market = scam" — these are the canonical scam fingerprints.
  • Pre-2006 vehicles (1997 Coleshill Hilux, 2000 Beaminster Hilux, 2000 Alton Hilux, 2000 Brentwood Hilux, 2002 Bradford L200, 2004 Pulborough Ranger, 2004 Spalding Ranger, 2004 Newbury Ranger, 2004 Worcester Ranger XLT, 2005 Bradford Hilux VX, 2005 Penzance Hilux, 2005 Gravesend Hilux) — exceed 20-year age limit.

docs.title: Pattern: UK Hiluxes are structurally rotten at this price point
docs.text:
All three Toyota Hiluxes in this search that were MOT-checked had catastrophic structural corrosion: - GF11 THG (2011, 1 owner, full history): sills corroded through, seat belt anchor holed - SM61 OLO (2011, 10 service stamps): chassis in poor condition, sills holed, all body mountings corroded - WU07 TXL (2007): brake pipes corroded throughout, fuel tank strap rotted off

Toyota engines are mechanically excellent (2KD-FTV is gold standard) but the bodies do not survive UK salt exposure. At the sub-£5,500 price point, any Hilux old enough to be affordable is old enough to be structurally compromised.

docs.title: L200s fare better structurally
docs.text:
• DG56 ORJ (2006, 20 years old): NO structural corrosion in 26 MOT tests
  • KY62 VOH (2013): NO structural corrosion in 8 tests

docs.title: Ground Clearance Comparison
docs.text:
Platform Vehicles CarsGuide (mm) Manufacturer (mm) Verdict Renault Trafic Gen 2 (X83) AE14SVG, SY12TXD — ~160 HIGHEST — best for rough roads Citroen Dispatch Gen 2 (Sevel Nord) GRZ8768, SY64XXH, KU14OAP, WN14NYW 150 ~150 Good — higher than Vivaro/Transit Renault Trafic III / Vivaro (X82) DS68SYG, AF67LWH, DU65MKG, KU68VPN, MJ66YGG, MT16YZP, EG68HTT, DM19KXT 127 ~160 Mid-range — CarsGuide may measure differently Ford Transit Custom (V362) SV15HZM, LK14BGU 118 ~150 LOWEST — worst for rough roads

Key finding: The Citroen Dispatch does NOT have the lowest ground clearance — at 150mm it's actually higher than the Transit Custom (118-150mm) and comparable to Vivaro/Trafic (127-160mm). The old-shape Trafic Gen 2 (SY12TXD, AE14SVG) has the best clearance at ~160mm.

Note on measurements: CarsGuide measures consistently across brands (good for relative comparison) but may measure at the lowest body point (bumper/aero). Manufacturer specs typically measure at the lowest mechanical point (axle/sump). Actual clearance under load with 9 passengers will be lower than unladen specs.

docs.title: Notes & Observations
docs.text:
1. GRZ8768 (#1) re-confirmed available 2026-04-12 at the same £3,750 price. The rerun + Facebook pass surfaced no candidate that beats it on the fundamentals (92k, 1 owner 9 yrs, 11-test perfect MOT, £2,750 under budget). It remains the strong buy.

  2. Market is tight for Trafic-size 9-seaters under £6k. Most are £7k+ with reasonable mileage. Best value is coming from eBay/Gumtree/Facebook rather than AutoTrader dealers.

  3. Citroen Dispatch is the standout platform. PSA 2.0 HDi (DW10) is proven, has massive remaining life, and timing belt is the main item to verify. Five 2014 Dispatches now in the pool — if GRZ8768 falls through, the £5,995 Carlisle one (1 owner, 90k, FSH) has the closest spec.

  4. R9M 1.6 CDTi appears across most Vivaro/Trafic candidates. Acceptable engine but known for timing chain issues at high mileage. Watch out for chain rattle / oil pressure complaints.

  5. Worcester dealer "lightwoodvans" appear to have sold their Vivaros as a batch. DS68SYG, DU65MKG (and originally AF67LWH) are absent from the current AutoTrader Vivaro minibus search — but AF67LWH is still alive on Facebook at £6,495, in budget under the new cap. Phone 01905 975 415.

  6. AE14SVG is dual-listed. Same vehicle (reg confirmed via masked AutoTrader plate A****VG) is on Facebook at £6,500 and AutoTrader at £7,475 (seller price hunting). AutoTrader still shows MOT expired despite seller's "12mth mot" claim — insist on a fresh MOT certificate before any commitment.

  7. EcoBlue wet-belt is close to a hard disqualifier. Per the buyer manual, the Transit/Tourneo 2.0 EcoBlue wet belt is a known catastrophic fault. The 2018/68 Liverpool Tourneo at 187k (backup pool) only deserves pursuit with a documented wet-belt + water-pump replacement receipt.

  8. Ford Transit Custom new-listings are all £9k+ in this size class. The 2.2 TDCi (chain-driven, pre-EcoBlue) is the best Ford engine and only appears in older year/higher mileage examples (SV15HZM, LK14BGU, the Portsmouth backup-pool find).

  9. VW Transporter shuttles were not found under £6,500 in 9-seat configuration.

  10. The Portsmouth Tourneo Custom Limited (756140874188702, backup pool) is the highest-leverage next investigation. Same engine family as #7 SV15HZM but with 73k fewer miles and £955 cheaper, only 50mi from Brighton. The only blocker is a privacy-blurred plate — getting the reg from the dealer (07831 148354) is the single most valuable next step.

docs.title: MOT Pattern Analysis
docs.text:
• Failure rate: 5 failures in 16 tests (31% overall). But 5 failures in 10 tests since heavy use began (50%).
  • Recurring issues:
  • Track rod ends — failed at tests #2, #4, #6 (and possibly #9, #11). This is chronic. Either cheap replacement parts or alignment issue causing premature wear.
  • Anti-roll bar bushes/links — advisory or failure across multiple tests. Expected at this mileage but frequent.
  • Driveshaft oil seal leak — advisory at tests #3, #4, #5. Chronic, not repaired.
  • Brake wear — dangerous at test #6 (pads <1.5mm). Brakes run to destruction rather than proactively replaced.
  • Tyre neglect — dangerous at test #6 (cords exposed on 2 tyres). Tyres run until cords show. Repeated front tyre wear advisories.
  • Structural corrosion: None found in any test. Positive.
  • Brake system: Dangerous brake pad condition at Jul 2024. Multiple worn brake disc/pad advisories across tests. Pattern of running brakes to failure rather than proactive replacement.
  • Emissions: "emissions no peak detected" advisory noted. Could indicate DPF issue or just testing anomaly.
  • Inspector notes: "Engine cover and undertrays fitted restricting view" — noted at multiple tests. The underside of the engine was not fully visible to inspectors.

docs.title: Key Concern: Maintenance Philosophy
docs.text: The MOT pattern tells a clear story: from 2022 onwards, this vehicle was driven extremely hard (~55k mi/yr) with reactive rather than proactive maintenance. Items were fixed only when they failed MOT, not before. The dangerous defects at Jul 2024 (exposed tyre cords, dangerously thin brake pads) are not just wear — they indicate the vehicle was driven in an unsafe condition. For a 9-seater carrying passengers, this is concerning.

docs.title: Reliability Assessment
docs.text:

  • DPF status: Has DPF (Euro 6, ULEZ compliant). DPF not a concern for Ukraine highway use.
  • Known model issues: NV300 = rebadged Renault Trafic III. Same R9M engine, same platform, same everything. Timing chain is the main concern at this mileage.
  • Timing belt/chain: R9M uses a timing CHAIN (not belt). Known weak point. At 224k miles, chain stretch is likely. Replacement cost: £800-1,500. Must be inspected.
  • Clutch: Just replaced (clutch kit + dual-mass flywheel, £1,000 with receipt). Positive — this is a major service item done.
  • Gearbox: Driveshaft oil seal leak is chronic. Minor now but may worsen.

docs.title: Critical Market Insight
docs.text:
There are effectively NO armoured CIT vans available for private purchase on the UK domestic market. This is not a search failure — it is a market reality:

  1. UK security companies (G4S/Allied Universal, Loomis, Brinks) dispose of decommissioned CIT vehicles through specialist dealers
  2. These specialist dealers (primarily Gericia International in London) are contractually or regulatorily restricted from selling CIT vehicles within the UK or Ireland
  3. All UK-based CIT vehicles are export-only
  4. The mainstream used vehicle platforms (AutoTrader, eBay, Gumtree) have zero armoured vehicle listings

The realistic options are: - Buy from Gericia for export (their Sprinters are in London but marked "cannot be sold into UK/Ireland" — since the vehicle goes to Ukraine, export purchase may be possible) - Import from Europe (Germany has the most active market for used Geldtransporter/CIT vans)

docs.title: Conversion Considerations
docs.text: Converting a CIT van to passenger use requires: 1. Remove safes and cash-handling equipment from rear compartment 2. Install seats and seatbelts — the rear compartment has no seating 3. Add ventilation/heating to rear — CIT vans have sealed rear compartments 4. Emergency exit — CIT vans often have only one entry/exit point 5. Windows are NOT feasible — cutting through armored panels is extremely difficult and compromises protection. Passengers would ride in an enclosed compartment (acceptable for short evacuation runs) 6. Weight consideration — armored vehicles are significantly heavier than standard vans. The Fiat Ducato B6 likely weighs 3.5-4 tonnes empty.
